_comment: Fallout 4's own NIF layouts, layered over schemas/nif/base. Fallout 4 is 20.2.0.7 with user version 12 and bs_version 130 (nifgen's is_v20_2_0_7_fo4). Measured against the meshes in Fallout4 - Meshes.ba2: every block below was checked byte for byte, and the vertex data's length was confirmed against data_size - num_triangles * 6. Fallout 4 uses the same BSVertexDataSSE packed vertex format as Skyrim SE, so the reader's unpacker is shared.

BSConnectPoint::Children.note: The child half of a connect point pair.

BSConnectPoint::Parents.note: Connect points define attachment points on meshes.

BSDynamicTriShape.note: A BSTriShape whose vertices the engine updates every frame: the same packed vertex block, then the dynamic copy of it.

BSFurnitureMarkerNode.note: A node that marks where furniture's markers sit. Each marker is a name and a position and a rotation, which the base's own structs describe.

BSLightingShaderProperty.note: Fallout 4 BSLightingShaderProperty layout (140 bytes base, 146 bytes with environment mapping).

BSMeshLODTriShape.note: Fallout 4 BSMeshLODTriShape adds 3 32-bit LOD sizes after BSTriShape (12 bytes).

BSTriShape.note: nif.xml's BSTriShape: Fallout 4 holds its vertices in the shape itself, in a packed format, where the original edition keeps them in a separate NiTriShapeData block. Measured: the data size is the vertex data's bytes plus the triangles' six bytes each, so the vertex data is the data size less the triangles. The vertex description's low nibble is the vertex's size in four-byte words, and its next nibbles are the word offsets of the UV, the normal, the tangent and the colour; bits 44 and up are the VertexAttribute flags that say which of those fields are present. The packed vertices themselves are read by the NIF reader, not by the schema: their layout is a function of the description, and the schema language has no way to say 'a field whose size another field decides'.

NiAVObject.note: Same as the base's, written out here so this file stands on its own: bs_version 130 is above 34, so the property list is gone, and 20.2.0.7 is above 67240448, so the velocity vector is gone too. What is left is the flags, the transform and the collision object.

NiGeometry.note: Fallout 4 NiGeometry drops material_data (nif.xml: Material Data vercond #BS_LT_130#).

NiLight.note: nif.xml: In Fallout 4 (bs_version 130), NiLight inherits directly from NiAVObject, dropping NiDynamicEffect's switch_state and affected_nodes.

NiNode.note: The node effects list is a pre-Fallout-4 field: nifgen's NiNode yields num_effects and effects only when bs_version < 130, and Fallout 4 (bs_version 130) drops it entirely.

NiParticleSystem.note: Fallout 4 NiParticleSystem layout: AVObject base, bounding sphere, skin, shader, alpha, vertex_desc, data_ref, flags_2, psys_data, has_modifiers bool, num_modifiers, modifiers.

bhkNPCollisionObject.note: Fallout 4 bhkNPCollisionObject (flags: u16, data: ref, body_id: u32).
